stories.title: ASP Anuj Chaudhary arrives in Gorakhpur, offers prayers at temple:Yogi presents khichdi, smiles as child asks for chips
stories.summary: CM Yogi offered khichdi at the Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur on Thursday morning, marking the occasion of Makar Sankranti. Gorakshapitheshwar Yogi Adityanath entered the sanctum sanctorum at around 3:40 a.m. and, following the Nath tradition, performed special worship and rituals in honour of Guru Gorakhnath. He blew the traditional whistle hanging around his neck and bowed in reverence. After the rituals, khichdi was offered to Guru Gorakhnath, including the sacred offering sent by the Nepal Royal Family. CM tours temple premises Following the worship, the Chief Minister toured the temple premises and extended Makar Sankranti greetings to devotees. Soon after, the ritual of common devotees offering khichdi formally began. Temple echoes with sounds of drums On the festival day, lakhs of devotees from Nepal, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar thronged the Gorakhnath Temple. The entire temple complex echoed with the sound of drums and devotional chants. By 8 am, around three lakh devotees had already offered khichdi. Long queues were seen outside the temple, with devotees getting darshan after waiting for nearly an hour. See the pictures... Devotees offer khichdi Due to the massive crowd, many devotees were offering khichdi from outside the sanctum sanctorum. With hundreds of people offering rice, lentils, sesame seeds and other ingredients simultaneously, it appeared as though grains were raining across the temple premises. Devotees from Nepal to participate Thousands of devotees arrived from Nepal to participate in the ritual. They said offering khichdi at Gorakhnath Temple on Makar Sankranti is an age-old tradition in their country, as Baba Gorakhnath is regarded as their revered deity. To manage the crowd and ensure smooth arrangements, temple volunteers along with police and administrative personnel were deployed at various points across the premises.

stories.title: Husband, wife found running sex racket from Varanasi house:Man flees during police raid, spouse arrested; boys, girls found unclothed
stories.summary: A husband and wife were allegedly operating a sex racket from their residence in Varanasi, using a spa centre as a cover. The operation was busted after police conducted a raid on Wednesday. During the raid, several young men and women were found without clothes. Two young men and a young woman were caught in objectionable circumstances, and multiple objectionable items were recovered from one of the rooms. Police forced open the doors of two rooms and arrested the spa centre owner along with two women and two men. Investigations revealed that the spa was being run jointly by the woman and her husband. However, the accused husband managed to escape from the spot during the police action. The spa centre was operating from Maqbool Alam Road in the Cantonment area. Despite being located close to the police officers’ residential colony, its activities had gone unnoticed. Acting on information provided by local residents, ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja led the raid with a police team, which exposed the illegal operation. Know about the entire matter in sequential order... Now know how it was exposed ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja said - Neighbors informed about running a sex racket in the house. The police team conducted a raid. As soon as the raid happened, Sameer Siddiqui fled from the spot. His wife Tarannum was caught by us. One boy and two girls were found in objectionable condition in one room. Then police started searching other rooms. Two rooms were locked. When police broke the locks, liquor bottles and objectionable items were found inside. Suspects are being interrogated According to police, currently the accused woman Tarannum and the arrested young man and woman are being interrogated. Their previous criminal records are also being investigated. ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja said- Police is constantly monitoring such activities. No one will be allowed to be above the law.

stories.title: Chaos at Mayawati press conference after short circuit:Smoke fills hall, panic erupts; BSP supremo leaves without taking questions or cutting cake
stories.summary: Chaos broke out during a press conference addressed by Mayawati on Wednesday when a short circuit occurred in a ceiling light at the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) office in Lucknow. Sparks were seen, and the hall quickly filled with smoke. Party workers present in the conference hall panicked as the situation unfolded. Security personnel immediately stepped in and used fire extinguishers to bring the situation under control. The press conference was called off soon after. Mayawati left the venue without cutting the cake and without taking questions from the media. Earlier, the BSP chief had made a strong statement on a recent meeting of BJP’s Brahmin legislators. She said the Brahmin community did not need “bati-chokha” from anyone but wanted respect. She added that if the BSP came to power, the aspirations of the Brahmin community would be fulfilled. She also cautioned Brahmins not to fall for the influence of the Congress, BJP or the Samajwadi Party. Speaking on the party’s electoral strategy, Mayawati made it clear that the BSP would contest all elections across the country on its own. She said the party would go solo in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections as well, and there should be no confusion on this issue. The remarks came in the backdrop of a meeting of BJP’s Brahmin MLAs held during the Assembly session. BJP’s state president Pankaj Chaudhary had expressed displeasure, calling the meeting a violation of party discipline. He had said he spoke to the MLAs individually and would take action. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had also taken a dig at the BJP. Referring to a New Year gathering, he remarked that BJP MLAs were sitting and eating litti-chokha, and questioned what would happen if they turned against the government. He sarcastically added that the BJP was now even investigating bati-chokha. Two key points from Mayawati’s press conference 1. Caste-based parties must change their mindset On alliances, Mayawati said a positive decision could be considered in the future only if caste-based parties abandoned casteist thinking and were able to transfer upper-caste votes to the BSP. However, she said this would take years, and until such a change happened, the BSP would not think of alliances. 2. No room for complacency in UP elections She alleged that the BJP, Congress and SP were using every possible tactic to weaken the BSP. A strong response was necessary, she said, and bringing the party to power in Uttar Pradesh was essential. She asserted that the people wanted the BSP in power and the party would leave no stone unturned in the upcoming elections. What was the meeting of Brahmin MLAs about? On December 23, a meeting of Brahmin MLAs was held in Lucknow during the winter session of the विधानसभा. The gathering, attended by BJP MLAs and some SP rebels, took place at the Lucknow residence of Kushinagar BJP MLA P. N. Pathak, officially on the occasion of his wife’s birthday. Around 45–50 Brahmin MLAs from Purvanchal and Bundelkhand attended the meeting, where litti-chokha and vrat food were served. After the meeting, political circles were abuzz. Sources said the Chief Minister’s OSD contacted Pathak, who maintained that it was only a community meal and not a political meeting. Senior RSS and BJP leaders were also said to be involved in defusing the situation. Why was the meeting held? Sources said the MLAs felt that while several castes had become powerful in caste-based politics, Brahmins were being sidelined. They alleged that Brahmin issues were being ignored and that despite having a deputy chief minister from the community, real power was lacking. The meeting was aimed at raising Brahmin concerns more assertively. Political analysts point out that although Brahmins constitute around 11–12 per cent of Uttar Pradesh’s population, they play a decisive role in nearly 30 districts. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP received about 89 per cent of Brahmin votes. The BSP had successfully used a Brahmin–Dalit social engineering formula in 2007 to come to power with a full majority under Mayawati. However, shifts in political alignment over the years saw Brahmin voters moving from the BSP to the SP in 2012 and later backing the BJP in 2017, when the party formed a full-majority government with significant Brahmin representation in the Assembly.

stories.title: Devotees rush Ganga Ghats of Kashi on Makar Sankranti:Take holy dip, offer Khichdi to Baba Vishwanath, donate food, clothes and money; city police on alert
stories.summary: A flood of devotion surged at the banks of Mother Ganga on Makar Sankranti festival on Thursday. Since early morning on Makar Sankranti, the atmosphere became devotional with chants of Har Har Gange, Namami Gange, Namami Mate. Devotees took holy dips in the Ganges, performed worship in temples, and earned spiritual merit by donating food, clothes, and money. By 10 AM, more than 3 lakh people had reached the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Ganga Ghats. Crowds were visible at various ghats of Kashi including Dashashwamedh Ghat, Sheetala Ghat, Panchganga Ghat, Assi Ghat, and up to Ganga Gotami Sangam Kaithi since morning, where people took holy baths and performed charitable acts. Meanwhile, the sequence of darshan and worship continues at Baba Darbar, and devotees also visited the Khichdi Baba Temple to receive the prasad of khichdi. See the pictures.... Police administration on alert on water and land For the safety of devotees coming to bathe in the Ganges on Makar Sankranti, 100 personnel on 25 boats are on alert. These include personnel from Water Police, NDRF, and PAC Flood Unit. Main ghats have been barricaded. Police from local stations are also deployed at the ghats. Police and administration are fully alert regarding the safety of devotees from the ghat to the Ganges. Importance of Makar Sankranti Pandit Vikas explained - Black gram (urad dal) has special significance on Makar Sankranti. That's why on this day khichdi is made by mixing black gram and rice, and it is offered to God. Along with this, donating khichdi is also beneficial. Besides khichdi, one must offer arghya to Sun God with black sesame seeds on this day. Along with this, donations of sesame seeds, jaggery, clothes, blankets etc. should also be made. Doing this brings the blessings of Sun God. It also brings happiness and prosperity in life. Entry through 5 gates at Kashi Vishwanath Temple After bathing at Baba Vishwanath's abode, people are arriving to offer khichdi while some are coming for darshan. The temple administration is allowing entry through 5 gates. The Chief Executive Officer said - our priority is that devotees should not have to stand in line for long, so adequate barricading has been done. Today the protocol is closed and touch darshan is also not being allowed. Performed aarti of Mother Ganga and Lord Surya on Makar Sankranti On the auspicious occasion of Makar Sankranti for nature conservation remembrance, Namami Gange performed aarti of the sun of Sanatan and Mother Ganga, the goddess of nature, while wishing for joy, harmony and environmental protection. Under the coordination of Rajesh Shukla, Namami Gange Kashi region coordinator and cleanliness brand ambassador of Municipal Corporation, the message of preservation of culture and nature was given through national flags and boards with cleanliness slogans.

stories.title: ‘No place for non-believers in India, their place is Pakistan’:Satua Baba makes provocative statement at Magh Mela; denies owning any luxury possessions while seated in a Porsche
stories.summary: “There is no place for non-believers in India. Their place is Pakistan. They should leave on time because the Rafale of development has already taken off here.” These remarks were made by Satua Baba, who often remains in the spotlight during the Magh Mela. Satua Baba has also drawn attention for his frequent use of luxury vehicles. On January 14, he reportedly stopped using his ₹3-crore Land Rover Defender and arrived in a Porsche 911 Turbo, said to be worth around ₹4.40 crore. Speaking to Bhaskar, Satua Baba said he has no attachment to luxury cars. “I don’t have any passion for these vehicles. I only know that if I sit in a car, it should take me to Kashi, Prayagraj or Ayodhya. That is all,” he said. He added that he does not know the names or prices of the cars he travels in and joked that “Google Baba” knows more about them. Q: You said there is no place for non-believers in India and that they should go to Pakistan. What did you mean? Satua Baba: Those who do not believe in India and Sanatan should understand that India is moving ahead. The Rafale of development has already taken off here. Those who do not connect with this thought will not find a place here. Q: You are often seen changing luxury vehicles. Recently, you arrived in a Porsche after using a Land Rover Defender. Why? Satua Baba: I do not have any passion for vehicles. I only know that a car should take me from one place to another. If I sit in a car in Kashi, it should take me to Prayagraj. If I leave from here, it should take me to Ayodhya. That is my only concern. Q: Do you know the price or features of these cars? Satua Baba: No. I do not know their names, features or prices. For that, there is Google Baba. I only know how to sit in a vehicle and reach my destination. Q: Many people question how a saint can travel in such expensive cars. What is your response? Satua Baba: Can spirituality not travel in these cars? Is Sanatan so weak that it will be misunderstood because of a vehicle? This is the speed of Sanatan. Those who tried to divide Sanatan and those who fired bullets at Ram will be crushed at this speed. Q: On Wednesday, you reached the Magh Mela in a Porsche. Was that intentional? Satua Baba: No. For me, a cart, a jeep, a Bullet, a JCB or a luxury car are the same. The goal is only to reach where I have to go and continue my work. Q: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said from the stage that people should connect with you. How do you see that statement? Satua Baba: It was not meant for me personally. It was for the ascetic form. Whoever connects with Sanatan connects with India. Q: You are seen meeting political and administrative figures at your ashram. Does that affect your spiritual role? Satua Baba: I meet everyone, but my main focus is on the Kalpavasis staying in the ashram. Serving devotees is my first duty. Q: What responsibility have you taken at the Magh Mela? Satua Baba: Satua Ashram is the largest ashram at the Magh Mela. Devotees keep coming with faith. It is the duty of a saint to give them shelter and support. We are doing that. Q: You praised the current government while speaking about development. What did you mean? Satua Baba: Those who did not give light to the poor, food to the hungry, or roads to the people are gone. This is Prime Minister Modi and Yogi’s India. Development will now move faster. Q: What message do you give to devotees coming to the Magh Mela? Satua Baba: Come with faith and devotion. Take a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam. Unite your family and society. India is now being discussed across the world. After 500 years, Ram reached Ayodhya, and the country is moving forward.

stories.title: After losing to Indira, Raj Narain claimed vote theft evidence:How a fierce election dispute triggered disqualification, emergency rule reshaped India’s national politics forever
stories.summary: From today begins The 'Rajneeti ki Rangbhoomi', a special series that chronicles the great political 'Mahabharata' of Uttar Pradesh, a battlefield where every move by leaders creates history. This series explores clashing ideologies, broken alliances, new friendships, dissolving factions and ever-shifting power equations. In the very first episode, we revisit one of the most dramatic political confrontations in Indian history, Raj Narain versus Indira Gandhi. Why did Raj Narain become a persistent thorn in Indira Gandhi’s path? How did this man eventually cause her disqualification, electoral defeat and the declaration of the Emergency? December 1970: A Political Earthquake in Delhi December 1970 was sending chills through Delhi’s power corridors. The political tension inside Rashtrapati Bhavan spilled out and scorched the entire nation. Suddenly, the news broke- 'The Lok Sabha has been dissolved. Elections will be held one year early.' The announcement exploded like a bomb in the opposition camp. In a smoke-filled secret room, senior opposition leaders gathered. One leader exhaled cigar smoke and remarked calmly,' Madam has played a masterstroke.' Another shot back sharply, 'If we fight alone, we will be chopped like vegetables.' 'So what’s the solution?' a third asked. After a brief silence, a single voice answered,' We fight together.' Congress splits: R Versus O The roots of this confrontation lay in 1969, when senior Congress leaders fell out with Indira Gandhi and expelled her from the party. Congress split into two factions. Indira’s faction was named Congress (R), R for Revolutionary. The old guard became Congress (O), O for Organisation. Both factions fought elections against each other. Congress (O)’s symbol was a woman spinning a charkha, while Congress (R) was allotted the cow and calf. As elections approached, Congress (O), Jan Sangh and the Socialists joined hands. The battle was no longer electoral, it was about proving who represented the 'real Congress'. Raebareli question: Indira stands firm On December 29, a packed press conference hall awaited Indira Gandhi. A journalist asked pointedly, 'Madam Prime Minister, is it true you may leave Raebareli and contest from Gurgaon?' The hall fell silent. Indira replied firmly. 'No.' 'Any particular reason?' the journalist pressed. 'I am not doing that. That is enough,' she said curtly. January 1971: The Search for a Challenger On January 19, opposition leaders met secretly again. One crucial question loomed, who would challenge Indira Gandhi in Raebareli? The answer echoed through the room: Raj Narain. One leader struck the table.'This man can keep power awake at night.' 'But will he agree?' someone asked. 'He fears no defeat,' came the reply. The contest was set, Raj Narain versus Indira Gandhi. This was no longer an election. It was war. Campaign sparks and sarcasm Indira Gandhi addressed a massive rally in Coimbatore. When Raj Narain’s name surfaced, a faint smile crossed her face. She declared sharply, 'The opposition has no face.' A voice from the crowd shouted,'And Raj Narain?' Indira retorted sarcastically, 'In Raebareli they have fielded someone who survives on criticism. He only knows how to shout against Nehruji.' Voting day and a crushing defeat Voting took place on March 7, 1971. Counting lasted days. Even before counting began, Raj Narain took out a victory procession on March 8, shouting,'This is democracy’s victory!' But on March 10, the tables turned. Congress (R) swept Raebareli. Indira Gandhi: 1,83,309 votes Raj Narain: 71,499 votes A margin of over 1.10 lakh. Raj Narain was stunned. 'This is impossible, those who marched with me, whom did they vote for?' The rumour of 'Magic Ink' Soon, whispers spread across Raebareli, of 'magic ink'. A supporter told Raj Narain,'This wasn’t voting, Netaji, it was chemistry.' 'What do you mean?' Raj Narain asked. 'They say the ink vanished, and the Congress symbol reappeared before counting.' 'If this is true,' Raj Narain replied grimly, 'I will drag this ink to court.' Taking the PM to Court In April 1971, Raj Narain approached Allahabad lawyer Ramesh Srivastava. 'I want to drag Indira to court,' he declared. 'You are challenging the Prime Minister,' the lawyer warned. 'There is no Prime Minister in law,' Raj Narain replied. 'Only a culprit.' Shanti Bhushan was brought in. He initially dismissed the 'magic ink' claim as absurd but later reframed it as mechanical fraud. A 258-page petition was drafted, listing eight serious charges, from misuse of government machinery to exceeding election expenditure limits. 'If even one is proven,' Shanti Bhushan warned, 'the Prime Minister will be in trouble.' June 12, 1975: The Verdict After four years of hearings, June 12, 1975 arrived. At 1 Safdarjung Road, PM’s residence, tension was unbearable. Teleprinters rattled. Inside Courtroom No. 24 of the Allahabad High Court, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha read the verdict calmly. Mrs Gandhi was found guilty of two corrupt practices, including using government officer Yashpal Kapoor in her campaign. At 10:20 am, UNI flashed the headline: 'Indira Gandhi Unseated.' Rajiv Gandhi informed his mother.'Mummy, they have disqualified you.' She replied quietly, 'So they finally did it.' Pressure, defiance and the Emergency Opposition leaders demanded resignation. Indira chose defiance. On June 25, JP’s rally at Ramlila Maidan thundered. Raj Narain declared,'Tomorrow we will gherao her residence.' That night, Emergency was imposed. Raj Narain was arrested at dawn. Opposition leaders were jailed. Parliament passed the 39th Amendment, barring courts from challenging the Prime Minister’s election. 1977: The Final Reckoning After 19 months, elections were announced. Raj Narain refused to contest from a 'safe seat'.'I will fight only from Raebareli,' he said. Campaigning fiercely, he attacked elitism and arrogant power. When the results were declared, history turned full circle. Raj Narain: 1,77,719 votes (52%) Indira Gandhi: 1,22,517 votes (35.7%) The man who once lost by over a lakh votes had returned to unseat the most powerful leader in the country. *** References The Case That Shook India: The Verdict That Led to the Emergency - Prashant Bhushan | Emergency Retold - Kuldip Nayar | Emergency Chronicles: Indira Gandhi and Democracy's Turning Point - Gyan Prakash | Raj Narain: Not Just a Name, History - Shahnawaz Ahmad Qadri | Raj Narain: The Path of Thought - Dhirendra Srivastava | State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain (Allahabad High Court Verdict) Individuals: Prof. Anand Kumar, Suresh Khairnar, Vijay Vidrohi, Dhirendra Srivastava, Shahnawaz Ahmad Qadri. Creative liberty has been used to make the story interesting.

stories.title: Dimple Yadav simplicity stands apart in noisy Indian politics:Journey of daughter-in-law of UP's biggest political family reflects restraint, discipline and quiet influence
stories.summary: While Indian politics is increasingly dominated by spectacle, luxury, and grand displays, there is one woman who remains far removed from this culture. She keeps herself away from controversies and excess, and her simplicity is often cited as exemplary, truly understated in every sense. She is Dimple Yadav, the wife of Akhilesh Yadav, the leading figure of Uttar Pradesh’s most prominent political family. Carrying forward the legacy of Mulayam Singh Yadav’s Lok Sabha seat, Mainpuri, she is currently serving her second term as MP from the constituency. She has also represented the Kannauj Lok Sabha seat twice. On her birthday today, her life and choices once again draw attention for all the right reasons. See 2 photos from her wedding- Simplicity in action Dimple Yadav is neither fond of jewellery nor display. An incident from March last year illustrates this clearly. While travelling from Mainpuri to Lucknow, she came across an accident involving two cars. Police and emergency help were delayed, and tensions were rising between the two parties involved. Dimple stepped out of her vehicle, calmed both sides, and ensured they were taken to hospitals. Notably, she arranged for them to be sent to different hospitals to prevent any further confrontation. It was a quiet intervention, without cameras or statements, characteristic of her approach to public life. Dimple stepped out of her vehicle, calmed both sides, and ensured they were taken to hospitals. Notably, she arranged for them to be sent to different hospitals to prevent any further confrontation. It was a quiet intervention, without cameras or statements, characteristic of her approach to public life. When a diamond necklace was returned Her indifference to jewellery is well known within political circles. In 2021, a leader visiting the Yadav residence brought an imported diamond necklace as a gift for Dimple. Akhilesh Yadav asked what the gift was and, upon seeing it, responded pointedly. 'Have you ever seen her wearing jewellery?' he asked. 'Do not spoil her habits. She has no interest in these things. Take it back.' The necklace was returned, reinforcing Dimple Yadav’s preference for simplicity over luxury. Staying away from controversies Dimple Yadav has consistently kept herself distant from political controversies. Even when faced with sensitive questions, her responses, or silence, reflect restraint. In July 2025, during a visit by the Imam of the Parliament mosque along with Samajwadi Party leaders, Dimple was also present. Some clerics questioned her presence, triggering a brief debate. Dimple chose not to respond publicly and stayed away from the controversy altogether, maintaining her long-held approach of not engaging in unnecessary disputes. Army upbringing Born in Pune in 1978, Dimple Yadav comes from a disciplined Indian Army family. Her father, Colonel Ram Chandra Singh Rawat, is a retired army officer, and her mother is Champa Rawat. Originally from Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district, her family’s postings meant she spent her childhood across Pune, Bathinda, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lucknow. She studied at Army Public School, Lucknow, and later graduated in Commerce from Lucknow University. The army environment instilled discipline, self-reliance, and simplicity. Horse riding has been a passion since childhood, and she trained regularly at the Lucknow Racecourse and Cavalry Club. Love story against odds Dimple and Akhilesh Yadav’s love story reads like a film script. They met at a friend’s house in Lucknow, and at the time, Dimple was unaware that Akhilesh was Mulayam Singh Yadav’s son. Friendship grew into love over four years, even enduring Akhilesh’s time studying in Australia. Initially, both families were opposed to the marriage, partly due to caste differences and political circumstances linked to the Uttarakhand movement. It was Akhilesh’s grandmother, Murti Devi, whose approval eventually brought acceptance. The couple married on 24 November 1999 in Lucknow, in a ceremony attended by figures such as Amitabh Bachchan and Rajesh Khanna. Politics, family, and public life After marriage, Dimple stayed away from politics for nearly a decade, focusing on her home and three children, daughters Aditi and Tina, and son Arjun. Gardening and family time remain her favourite pursuits. She entered electoral politics in 2009 from Firozabad but lost to Congress leader Raj Babbar. In 2012, following Akhilesh Yadav’s elevation as Chief Minister, she was elected unopposed from Kannauj in a by-election, becoming the first woman from Uttar Pradesh and the 44th person nationally to achieve this feat. She won again in 2014, lost in 2019, and returned strongly in 2022 from Mainpuri after Mulayam Singh Yadav’s death. She retained the seat in 2024. Even today, her understated presence in Parliament continues to draw attention, proof that simplicity still resonates in public life. stories.title: Vulgar social media content sparks cyber complaint in Agra:Mother files FIR against content creator; influencer with lakhs of followers under probe
stories.summary: A woman in Agra has lodged a complaint with the cyber police against a social media influencer after her children were allegedly exposed to obscene content while watching reels on her mobile phone. The woman said an inappropriate clip suddenly appeared on the screen, prompting her to immediately snatch the phone from the children. In her complaint, she named the Instagram user ID that was being watched, alleging that it regularly serves obscene videos. According to the complaint, some of the reels on the account have garnered up to 14 million views. The woman claimed that two Instagram accounts operate under the same name, each with around 4.5 lakh followers. The influencer is also said to have about 10,000 followers on Facebook. She alleged that several comments on the videos are highly objectionable and unfit for display, and that the reels feature explicit content with suggestive audio. Demanding swift action, the complainant urged the cyber police to take strict steps against the operator of the user ID to prevent children from being exposed to such content. See 2 pictures... Now read the full matter in detail… A woman in Agra has approached the cyber crime cell alleging that obscene content circulating on Instagram is having a harmful impact on children and society, after her own children were allegedly exposed to such material while watching reels on a mobile phone. The complainant, Ruby Tomar, a resident of Fatehabad Road under Tajganj police station limits, supplies Ayurvedic medicines. She said that on January 4, while visiting a beauty parlour in Kamla Nagar to deliver medicines, she noticed a woman watching reels on her phone when an obscene video suddenly appeared on Instagram. Shocked by the content, the woman immediately scrolled past the reel, remarking that such videos were having a dangerous effect on children and society. Ruby said a similar incident occurred the following day at her home. On January 5, her children were using Instagram while she was sitting nearby. After watching multiple reels for some time, the same influencer’s video allegedly appeared on the screen. She immediately took the phone away from the children and later visited the Instagram profile linked to the reel. According to her complaint, all the videos uploaded on the account contained obscene visuals, vulgar gestures and objectionable remarks about women, accompanied by suggestive audio. She alleged that such content promotes moral degradation and negatively influences young viewers. During her own inquiry, she claimed to have learnt that the woman creating the reels is a resident of Kamla Nagar in Agra. Ruby Tomar has since filed a formal complaint with the Agra cyber police station, demanding strict action. Police officials said efforts are under way to trace the Instagram ID, verify its operator and identify the woman behind the account.

stories.title: ₹50-crore illegal toll collection exposed at UP toll plaza:Samajwadi Party leader, toll owner jailed; party alleges BJP MLA’s role in arrest
stories.summary: A joint police–administration team in Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur district arrested four people, including a toll plaza owner, on January 9 for allegedly forcing tractor-trolleys to pay toll tax illegally. Superintendent of Police Sagar Jain said preliminary estimates suggest that nearly ₹50 crore was collected unlawfully in a single year. “We are scrutinising records of the past five years. The actual amount could be higher,” he said. The main accused, toll plaza owner Kamaljeet Pradhan, is associated with the Samajwadi Party and is seeking the party ticket from the Nakud assembly seat. Following his arrest, Samajwadi Party leaders have alleged political vendetta, claiming that the arrest was orchestrated to protect the political future of the sitting Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Mukesh Chowdhary. Police officials, however, denied any political pressure and said the action was taken after complaints that tractor-trolleys were being stopped and forced to pay toll despite being exempt under rules. To understand the case, Bhaskar visited the site, spoke to police officers to learn how the alleged fraud was carried out, and held separate conversations with leaders from both parties. This report presents the full ground reality and political claims surrounding the controversy. First understand the complete case Toll owner among four arrested, fake receipts recovered The Saharanpur district administration cracked down on illegal toll collection at the Sarsawa toll plaza after District Magistrate Manish Bansal received complaints that ₹130 was being forcibly collected from every tractor-trolley, despite rules clearly exempting such vehicles from toll on national highways. Acting on the complaint, the DM formed a special team, which conducted a raid on January 9. The allegations were found to be correct. Following the raid, toll plaza owner Kamaljeet Pradhan, toll manager Kalu Singh Ranawat, and toll workers Akshay Kumar and Sagar were arrested. The team recovered one receipt book, eight torn receipts and three handwritten slips containing details of toll collections. An FIR was registered at Sarsawa police station on the complaint of regional accountant Ramprasad Gupta. On January 12, the Saharanpur Civil Court rejected the bail pleas of all four accused. ₹130 collected from every tractor-trolley To understand how the alleged fraud was carried out, we spoke to Saharanpur SP (Rural) Sagar Jain. He said ₹130 was being collected from each tractor-trolley using fake receipts printed at the toll operator’s level. “Farmers were given these receipts after money was taken. During initial questioning, the toll owner admitted that this illegal collection had been going on for about one year,” SP Jain said. Police estimate that illegal toll collection worth nearly ₹50 crore may have taken place during this period. “We are examining toll records of the past five years. All documents are under scrutiny, and further involvement of other individuals cannot be ruled out,” the SP added. Why so many tractor-trolleys pass through this toll Experts say the toll plaza became a lucrative point because Saharanpur is a major hub of the wood-carving and furniture industry. Poplar cultivation is widespread in the district, with over 50,000 farmers engaged in poplar farming. Neighbouring Yamunanagar in Haryana, which borders Saharanpur, has more than 350 plywood factories. Most of the poplar produced in Saharanpur and nearby Dehradun is transported to these factories. Due to intense competition, plywood companies have set up direct purchase counters in farmers’ fields, from where wood is transported daily by tractor-trolleys. The Sarsawa toll plaza lies on the only direct route to Yamunanagar factories. The highway also connects Dehradun with Panchkula, and mining tractor-trolleys operating along the Yamuna belt use the same route. Over 13,000 vehicles pass daily During an on-ground visit, toll employees, speaking off camera, said around 13,000 vehicles passed through the plaza daily last year, and the number has increased further. After the police action, toll collection from tractor-trolleys has been stopped. Most tractor-trolley drivers declined to speak on camera, citing fear and routine daily travel through the route. Political allegations surface The arrests have triggered political controversy. Leaders of the Samajwadi Party have alleged that Kamaljeet Pradhan, who is seeking the party ticket from the Nakud assembly seat, was arrested due to political vendetta. SP leaders claim the action was taken to benefit the sitting Bharatiya Janata Party MLA from Nakud, Mukesh Chaudhary. Social media campaigns in support of Kamaljeet began soon after his arrest, with several SP leaders calling the case politically motivated. Former SP district president Farhad Gada said the family claims Kamaljeet had no role in toll operations and that he went to the police station on his own after receiving a call from the SHO. He alleged the family was not informed before Kamaljeet was sent to jail. Gada also questioned why the administration allowed alleged illegal collection for a year if it was aware of the practice. Claim linked to SIR controversy Farhad Gada further alleged that Kamaljeet was targeted after he raised objections on social media regarding changes in assistant appointments during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work in Saharanpur, claiming names from a particular community were removed. He alleged this angered those in power and led to Kamaljeet’s arrest. Former BJP MLA raises questions Former BJP MLA Shashibala Pundir also questioned the arrest in social media posts, alleging Kamaljeet was falsely implicated. She said she met him in jail and claimed he had no current financial dealings with the toll plaza. She has sought an impartial investigation from the district administration. BJP MLA denies allegations Responding to allegations, BJP MLA Mukesh Chaudhary said Kamaljeet is like his nephew and had worked with him during elections. “Why would I get him arrested?” he said, denying any role in the action. Chaudhary said multiple leaders, including ministers and MLAs, had spoken to officials after the arrest. “The government order clearly states that toll cannot be collected from anything attached to a tractor. It has been confirmed that toll was being collected illegally,” he said. Police maintain that the investigation is based strictly on evidence and documents recovered during the raid, and that political affiliations will not affect the probe.

stories.title: Dense fog covers 30 districts of Uttar Pradesh:Temp drops to 3.1°C in Meerut; cars collide, over 50 trains delayed, weather likely to change soon
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is grappling with severe cold as icy winds continue to intensify the chill. Night temperatures have plunged below Shimla (7.2 degrees Celsius) and Jammu (4 degrees Celsius), marking one of the coldest periods this season. Dense fog hits 30 districts Since Thursday morning, dense fog has enveloped 30 districts, including Agra, Bareilly, Ghaziabad, Gonda, Hathras, and Sambhal. In several areas, visibility has dropped below 10 meters, leaving roads deserted and creating hazardous travel conditions. Transportation disruptions The thick fog has disrupted both rail and air travel. More than 50 trains, including VIP services like Vande Bharat, have been delayed. Around 10 flights also took off late due to poor visibility. In Meerut, two cars collided late at night due to the fog, leaving one driver critically injured. First, look at two pictures Temperature records across the state Over the past 24 hours, every district in the state recorded temperatures below 10 degrees Celsius. Meerut emerged as the coldest city at 3.1 degrees Celsius, followed by Ayodhya at 3.5 degrees Celsius, Muzaffarnagar at 4 degrees Celsius, and Hardoi-Raebareli at 4.2 degrees Celsius. Previous day’s fog-related incidents On Wednesday, dense fog affected 25 districts, including Meerut, Sambhal, and Bulandshahr. Low visibility led to three accidents involving six vehicles, resulting in one death and injuries to 20 people, including 15 schoolchildren. Weather forecast Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh stated, “Western winds will continue to affect the state over the next 5–6 days, causing minimum temperatures in many districts to drop by 4–6 degrees Celsius. From January 19, isolated rainfall with drizzle is expected in parts of western Uttar Pradesh.”

stories.title: 'You are insulting us by calling us Harijan,' shouts Mayawati:Moment that impressed Kanshi Ram, revealing unheard stories from ‘Behenji’s’ life on her 70th birthday
stories.summary: It was a cold December night in 1977 in Delhi’s Inderpuri area. Around 11 pm, someone knocked at the door of a small, dilapidated house. When the homeowner, Prabhu Das, opened the door, he saw a middle-aged man wearing worn-out clothes and a muffler around his neck. The man introduced himself: “I am the president of BAMCEF. I have come to invite your daughter to deliver a speech in Pune.” That man was Kanshi Ram, and he was speaking about Mayawati, Prabhu Das’s sixth child. That single meeting changed Mayawati’s life forever. A young woman preparing to become an IAS officer would later go on to become Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh four times. Her supporters would lovingly call her ‘Behenji’. Today is Mayawati's 70th birthday. On this occasion, read some unique stories from her life in Dainik Bhaskar... The speech that caught Kanshi Ram’s attention A day before Kanshi Ram visited her home, 21-year-old Mayawati had delivered a fiery speech at Delhi’s Constitution Club. The then Health Minister Raj Narain repeatedly addressed Dalits as “Harijan” in his speech. When Mayawati came to the stage, she shouted angrily: You are insulting us by calling us ‘Harijan’. Her sharp words made headlines in Delhi newspapers the next day. After reading those reports, Kanshi Ram went looking for her. At that time, Mayawati’s house had no electricity. She was studying under the light of a lantern, preparing for the civil services. From IAS dream to mass leader In his biography Kanshi Ram: Leader of Dalits, Badri Narayan writes that Kanshi Ram asked Mayawati what she wanted to become. She replied that she wanted to be an IAS officer to serve her community. Kanshi Ram responded: What will you do by becoming an IAS officer? I can make you a leader before whom many collectors will stand in line. Mayawati immediately understood where her future lay. Her father strongly opposed her decision and asked her to stop meeting Kanshi Ram or leave the house. Mayawati chose the movement, left home, and began living in the party office. Hardship, courage and early struggles Before entering politics, Mayawati worked as a school teacher in Delhi. She used her savings, packed a few clothes in a suitcase, and left home—an extraordinary step for a young woman at that time. She often travelled long distances on a bicycle with Kanshi Ram to expand the Dalit movement. In 1984, together they laid the foundation of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). A brave childhood incident Born on 15 January 1956 in Delhi, Mayawati was known for her courage from a young age. When she was in Class 5, her newborn brother fell seriously ill. With no one else available, Mayawati carried him 7 km on her shoulders to a government hospital. Doctors were stunned by the child’s determination. The speech that made her a mass leader In 1986, Mayawati delivered a historic speech in Haridwar, questioning decades of Dalit political exploitation. Her powerful questions and direct answers electrified the crowd. The impact was immediate. In 1989, she won her first Lok Sabha election. BSP’s vote share exceeded that of the BJP. From setbacks to power Mayawati lost her first two elections but made a strong comeback in 1989. She later became a Rajya Sabha MP and the leader of BSP’s parliamentary party. In 1995, after withdrawing support from Mulayam Singh Yadav’s government, the infamous Lucknow Guest House incident took place, where she was attacked by Samajwadi Party workers. That very night, with BJP’s support, Mayawati was sworn in as Uttar Pradesh’s first Dalit woman Chief Minister. She went on to serve as CM four times, achieving a full majority in 2007 through her strategy of social engineering. Why Mayawati gave up wearing sarees and long hair After facing humiliation and caste-based taunts in Parliament, Mayawati became extremely strict about cleanliness and discipline. She stopped wearing sarees and cut her long hair short to save time during hectic schedules. No one is allowed to enter her room wearing shoes—a rule shaped by her early experiences of discrimination. The vote that brought down Vajpayee’s government In 1999, Mayawati played a decisive role in Indian politics when the BSP voted against the Vajpayee government, causing it to fall by just one vote—one of the most dramatic moments in parliamentary history. Allegations, decline and attempted comeback Between 2007 and 2012, Mayawati faced corruption allegations, including the Taj Corridor and NRHM cases. BSP’s political influence declined sharply after 2012. However, in 2025, Mayawati signalled a comeback by appointing her nephew Akash Anand as the party’s number-two leader and mobilising massive crowds on Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary, keeping hopes alive for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. From a lantern-lit room to the Chief Minister’s office, Mayawati’s journey remains one of defiance, discipline, and determination in Indian politics.

stories.title: Ahilyabai Holkar statue damage sparks outrage from Kashi to Indore:Holkar Trust writes to Modi-Yogi to reinstall idols; administration say restoration work underway
stories.summary: The demolition of a portion of the historic Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi for the redevelopment work has faced severe backlash. The Ghat, an integral part of Kashi’s spiritual landscape, was originally built in 1771 by Malwa’s revered ruler, Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. Allegations that this nearly 250-year-old heritage structure was damaged under a cremation Ghat development project have triggered strong emotional reactions, stretching from Uttar Pradesh’s Kashi to Madhya Pradesh’s Indore. The anger is particularly intense in Indore and across the Malwa region, where Ahilyabai Holkar is deeply revered. Considered not merely a regional queen but a pan-Indian symbol of cultural renaissance and public welfare, any harm to her legacy is being seen as far more than a routine construction dispute—it has become an issue of heritage, faith, and identity. The project: ₹18 crore development, but at what cost to heritage? According to administrative records, a cremation Ghat development project worth around Rs 18 crore is underway in the Manikarnika Ghat area. The project’s foundation stone was laid in 2023 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi. Officials say construction is being carried out over approximately 29,350 square meters. Given the marshy soil along the Ganga’s banks, piling work was done up to a depth of 15–20 meters to reach stable soil, ensuring structural safety during floods. Damage to Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy sparks controversy The controversy erupted when portions of the Ghat associated with Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy were allegedly damaged during construction. Eyewitnesses and local residents claim that old stone steps were demolished and several historical idols and religious symbols linked to Ahilyabai Holkar were damaged. Some idols were reportedly buried under debris, while others were found lying in the open. There are also reports of damage to a Shivling. The demolished section reportedly housed idols connected to Ahilyabai Holkar’s devotion to Lord Shiva. Allegations state that these artifacts were neither properly protected nor was prior permission taken from any historical authority or trust. Holkar trust alleges sudden demolition without notice The Manikarnika Ghat is overseen by the private Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Charities Trust. Its president, Yashwantrao Holkar, has strongly objected to the action. In a letter, he said, With deep sorrow and disappointment, we inform that the historic Manikarnika Ghat of Varanasi has been suddenly demolished in the name of development. In 1791, Punyashlok Devi Ahilyabai Holkar had renovated this site. It held immense spiritual significance for her. He alleged that on January 10, 2026, without any prior notice, officials of the Varanasi Municipal Corporation ordered the demolition, which was completed within hours—completely ignoring the site’s historical and cultural importance. “The goddess honoured in Kashi, now buried in rubble” Yashwantrao Holkar further pointed out the irony that Prime Minister Modi himself had installed a statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar in the Kashi Vishwanath temple complex, honoring her as a great protector of Indian culture. “Yet, the sacred and historic idols associated with the same Ahilyabai Holkar now lie buried in debris at Manikarnika Ghat,” he wrote. The Trust has announced that it is taking immediate steps to recover and reinstall the damaged idols and is also considering legal action against the responsible authorities. Demands placed before the PM and CM The Holkar Trust and members of the Holkar royal family of Indore have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, raising the following demands: Social organizations express anger Following the incident, outrage has grown among social organizations in Indore. Groups representing the Dhangar, Pal, and Baghel communities have announced a meeting on January 15 to decide their future course of action. They argue that such treatment of Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy is unacceptable, especially when the nation has just concluded celebrations marking her 300th birth anniversary. Historians call it an attack on national heritage Senior historian Zafar Ansari termed the incident deeply distressing. “Devi Ahilyabai is not just the pride of Malwa or Maheshwar; she is a heritage figure for the entire nation. Every one of her works reflected foresight and public welfare,” he said. Ansari recalled that on May 31, 2025, the country celebrated Ahilyabai Holkar’s 300th birth anniversary. Prime Minister Modi visited Madhya Pradesh during the commemorations, inaugurated development projects in Bhopal, and released a commemorative postage stamp and a Rs 300 silver coin in her honor. Restoration funded by private royal property Historians also note that the temples and ghats built or restored by Ahilyabai Holkar were funded from her Khasgi (private royal property), not from the state treasury. The Holkar state maintained a distinct khasgi system, considered the queen’s personal wealth, through which hundreds of temples across India were built and preserved. Legal questions raised Experts point out that construction at a site like Manikarnika Ghat requires special caution under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. Strict regulations govern construction around historic and heritage sites. As a result, the issue has now moved beyond religious sentiment and public emotion, raising serious questions about administrative accountability and possible legal violations. About Manikarnika Ghat Manikarnika Ghat holds a unique place among Kashi’s 84 major ghats. According to legend, a jewel (Karnika) from Goddess Parvati fell here, giving the ghat its name. It is believed that cremation at this site grants liberation (Moksha). Devi Ahilyabai Holkar developed the ghat extensively, building Dharamshalas, temples, food centers, and bathing facilities for pilgrims. The ghat also shares a deep spiritual connection with the Kashi Vishwanath Dham. As the debate intensifies, authorities in Varanasi have stated that restoration work is underway. However, for many across Malwa and beyond, the incident has already struck a raw nerve—turning a development project into a national conversation on heritage, faith, and respect for history.

stories.title: RSS youth wing training held in Azamgarh:Om Prakash Rajbhar distributes yellow sticks uniforms to 2500 workers during training camp in Azamgarh
stories.summary: UP minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) national president Om Prakash Rajbhar has taken a major step to expand the Rashtriya Suheldev Sena (RSS), an organisation formed by his party. On Sunday, around 2,500 workers were given two-and-a-half-foot-long yellow sticks during a training programme held in Azamgarh. Participants were also provided with yellow uniforms of the organisation. Rajbhar referred to the sticks as “unlicensed weapons” and said the objective of the Rashtriya Suheldev Sena is to guide, train and create awareness among the youth so that they understand their rights and duties. First see 3 pictures of the event... What is the matter of stick distribution? In recent days, Om Prakash Rajbhar had announced the formation of a youth wing linked to the party, naming it Rashtriya Suheldev Sena (RSS). He had also spoken about providing “unlicensed weapons” to members of this force, which sparked widespread political discussion. Rajbhar arrived in Atraulia, Azamgarh, on Saturday and announced that RSS workers would be trained on Sunday and given unlicensed weapons. As a result, more than 2,500 young workers were called to the programme, where they received self-defence training under the supervision of retired Army officers. ‘Making society’s children aware’ Addressing the gathering, Rajbhar said that more than 60% of parents and children in society lack essential information. He added that many people are unaware of what kind of education is required for jobs in sectors such as education, police and health services. ‘Preparing RSS for the future’ Rajbhar said the Rashtriya Suheldev Sena would fight democratically against injustice, atrocities, corruption and exploitation. He added that members would also work in disaster situations and social problems through community service. He advised workers that if they come across an accident, they should help the injured reach the hospital instead of making videos. “This is humanity,” he said. Attack on Samajwadi Party During the programme, Rajbhar strongly criticised Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav. He alleged that when Akhilesh Yadav was Chief Minister, jobs were given only to people of his own caste and that he did not acknowledge Ahilyabai Holkar during his tenure. On the beautification work at Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi, Rajbhar said the BJP is focused on development and that the legacy of Ahilyabai Holkar will endure, along with the installation of a grand statue. Rajbhar has earlier advised party workers to wear yellow scarves and approach police stations collectively to present their cases. Leaders and districts represented

stories.title: Engineer dies after car falls into swamp in Noida:Screamed for help for 80 minutes; told father on phone, 'I don’t want to die'
stories.summary: A 27-year-old software engineer died after his car plunged into a 30-foot-deep, water-filled pit in dense fog in Noida late Friday night. The victim kept crying for help on the phone to his father for around 80 minutes before drowning. First see 4 pictures... What happened Yuvraj Mehta was driving from Gurugram to his residence at Tata Eureka Park, Sector-150, Noida, in his Grand Vitara. Near ATS Le Grand, his car broke through a drain wall at a U-turn and fell into a deep pit filled with drain water. The pit had been dug for a mall basement and later turned into a swamp. Desperate calls for help After the car began sinking, Yuvraj managed to climb onto its roof and called his father at around 12:20 am, saying, “Papa, save me. I don’t want to die.” His father alerted Dial-112 and rushed to the spot. Yuvraj remained just a few metres away, shouting with his phone torch on, but thick fog prevented visibility. Rescue delayed, victim drowned Police, fire brigade and later SDRF teams reached the site, followed by NDRF from Ghaziabad. However, due to zero visibility, cold water and iron rods in the pit, no one entered the water. Yuvraj kept screaming for help for nearly 80 minutes before drowning around 1:45 am. His body was recovered at about 4:30 am. Eyewitness account A delivery executive present at the scene said he saw Yuvraj flashing his mobile light and shouting, but neither police nor locals entered the swamp, citing dangerous conditions. The witness also attempted to help using a rope but failed due to fog and darkness. Family background Yuvraj’s father, Rajkumar Mehta, is a retired SBI director. His mother passed away a few years ago. His elder sister is married and lives in the UK. Yuvraj worked as a software engineer with Dunnhumby India in Gurugram. Negligence alleged Locals blamed the Noida Authority, saying multiple accidents had occurred earlier at the same spot due to lack of barricades and reflectors. After protests, the authority dumped debris near the site late at night. Case registered Joint CP Rajeev Narayan Mishra said an FIR has been registered at Knowledge Park police station against the plot owner following a complaint by the family. The incident is under investigation, and action will be taken against those found responsible.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Shinde faction seeks 2.5-year Mayor term, claim reports; bomb threat forces Indigo flight to make emergency landing in Lucknow more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Shinde faction seeks 2.5-year Mayor term, claim reports The BMC election results have created a fresh political deadlock in Maharashtra. The BJP has emerged as the single largest party in Mumbai, and there are clear indications that the BJP could get the mayor’s post for the first time. However, Eknath Shinde has shifted his 29 newly elected corporators to the Taj Lands End hotel in Bandra, where tight security has been deployed. 2. Bomb threat forces Indigo flight to make emergency landing in Lucknow A bomb threat on Indigo flight 6E-6650, en route from Delhi to Bagdogra, prompted an emergency landing at Lucknow Airport. Passengers were disembarked and the aircraft moved to an isolation bay after a note was found stuck on a bathroom napkin. 3. Millions expected at Mauni Amavasya snan as security tightened in Prayagraj An estimated three crore devotees are expected to take a holy dip at the Magh Mela today on Mauni Amavasya. Authorities have stepped up security and enforced city-wide traffic diversions after 1.5 crore people already bathed on January 17. 4. Thousands protest in Greenland; EU halts trade deal with US, calls emergency meeting as Trump’s 10% tariffs on 8 European countries Thousands of people took to the streets in Greenland to protest against US President Donald Trump. They expressed anger over his remarks about taking control of Greenland. Protesters shouted slogans like "Greenland is not for sale." 5. Clash at Prayagraj Magh Mela after police stop chariot procession A two-hour clash erupted between police and disciples of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand after officers halted a chariot procession. Several disciples were detained amid reports of one being dragged by the hair and beaten. 6. JEE aspirant in Prayagraj dies by suicide after recording apology video A student preparing for the Joint Entrance Exam in Prayagraj was found hanging at home after recording a final video apologising to his father. Police are investigating potential stress factors behind the tragedy. 7. Govt may announce more tax relief, health benefits ₹1 lakh standard deduction in Budget 2026 for senior citizens India's upcoming Union Budget 2026 might bring some welcome financial relief for senior citizens. According to Tarun Garg, a top executive at Deloitte India, the government might increase tax deductions for senior citizens, especially related to interest income and healthcare expenses. 8. Caste signalling intensifies ahead of UP Assembly elections in 2027 Events across UP, from family gatherings to Brahmin MLAs’ feasts and Rashtrakatha in Awadh, are increasingly seen as moves to consolidate political power. Attention is shifting to influential Kshatriya leaders, with comparisons being drawn between several key figures. 9. Dense fog causes multiple accidents in UP; flights diverted after circling Lucknow Heavy fog in Uttar Pradesh has reduced visibility to near zero, leading to ten accidents in one day, killing two and injuring 35. Flights were forced to circle over Lucknow before returning due to poor conditions. 10. Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa reveal their daughter’s name; writes ‘We introduce our greatest blessing, Parvati Paul Rao’ Bollywood actors Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa have officially announced the name of their new born daughter, sharing a heart-warming glimpse with their fans. The couple, who welcomed their first child in November 2025, named her Parvati Paul Rao, combining cultural significance with a personal touch.

stories.title: Chaos at Prayagraj Magh Mela after police stop chariot:Avimukteshwaranand's disciple detained, dragged by hair beaten as clash lasts 2 hours
stories.summary: A clash broke out between police and disciples of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, leading to pushing and shoving and a chaotic situation that lasted nearly two hours. Several disciples were taken into custody following the incident. See the pictures of Avimukteshwaranand's disciple being beaten... Police action on disciple caught on video Police detained one of Shankaracharya’s disciples and took him to a temporary outpost. A video accessed by Dainik Bhaskar shows the disciple arguing with policemen, after which the situation escalated. One policeman is seen pulling his hand, while another grabs his hair and pushes him. Inside the camp, the disciple was shoved to the ground, dragged by his hair and punched repeatedly. Throughout the incident, he could be heard screaming and pleading to be released. The identity of the detained disciple has not yet been confirmed. How the dispute began According to sources, the dispute began when police, citing heavy crowding, asked Shankaracharya to get down from his chariot and proceed on foot. The disciples refused and continued moving forward, leading to an argument that soon turned into pushing and shoving. Police officers attempted to defuse the situation and repeatedly requested cooperation, even folding their hands, but the disciples did not agree. Following this, the police took all supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Palanquin dragged, Shankaracharya alleges harassment

stories.title: BJP leader’s video with ₹500 note bundles surfaces:District minister Gautam Tiwari denies ownership; claims occult practitioners framed him using fake currency
stories.summary: A video allegedly showing a BJP leader surrounded by bundles of ₹500 notes has gone viral in Maharajganj district of UP. The video was reportedly recorded inside a room, where BJP district minister Gautam Tiwari can be clearly seen standing. In the footage, bundles of ₹500 notes are placed on a red carpet in one corner of the room. Gautam Tiwari is seen examining the bundles using the flashlight of his mobile phone. The person recording the video can be heard asking him to switch off the flashlight, saying that “Minister ji has already made a video.” More than 150 bundles of ₹500 notes More than 150 bundles of ₹500 notes are visible in the 20-second clip. However, the BJP leader has strongly denied that the money belongs to him. First 2 pictures- Money in video fake After the video surfaced, Gautam Tiwari spoke to journalists and rejected all allegations. He claimed that the incident was the result of a conspiracy involving people practising tantra-mantra (occult rituals). According to him, a group of five to six people cheated him of around ₹1.5 crore in the name of a land deal. He alleged that when he demanded the return of the money, they began blackmailing him by making a video using fake currency bundles, which he claimed were actually made of paper. However, he failed to clearly explain when and where the video was recorded. What Gautam Tiwari told media Reporter: A video is going viral showing bundles worth crores of rupees. You are also seen in it. What is the truth? Gautam Tiwari: The video was made by someone from Banaras. The money is fake and made of paper. This is the work of occult practitioners. Reporter: Are you being questioned or interrogated in the video? Gautam Tiwari: No, there was no interrogation. I have applied to an FIR. The money is fake. Reporter: You are claiming that about ₹1.5 crore was taken from you? Gautam Tiwari: Yes. Five or six people together took the money. I have filed a complaint at the police station. Reporter: What was the money given for? Gautam Tiwari: It was for a land deal. We are involved in the vegetable business. The money is stuck in Banaras, but it is not related to our business income. Reporter: Social media users are linking this money to hawala operations. Gautam Tiwari: That is completely false. There is no hawala case. The money shown in the video is not real. Reporter: Can you tell when and where the video was recorded? Gautam Tiwari: I cannot say exactly. I can only say that the money shown is fake. Reporter: Do you believe the matter is now clear? Gautam Tiwari: Yes. I have applied to an FIR. The police will investigate and take action. I want to live my life peacefully now. No complaint received yet When contacted, Kotwali Inspector Nirbhay Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that no formal complaint or application has been received so far regarding the matter. He said that if any written complaint is submitted, the police will investigate the case and take action as per the law.

stories.title: Mother clings to Major son’s coffin in Meerut:Says, 'My groom son is leaving'; brother sister cry uncontrollably
stories.summary: The body of Army Major Shubham Saini, who lost his life in a road accident near Dehradun, reached his home in Meerut on Sunday. The tragic incident occurred when his car lost control and plunged into a nearly 50-metre-deep gorge in Uttarakhand. After several hours of rescue efforts, Major Saini was pulled out of the gorge and rushed to the Dehradun Military Hospital in a critical condition. Doctors later declared him dead. The 27-year-old officer was posted in Chakrata, Uttarakhand, and was travelling to Dehradun on Saturday morning for official work. See 3 photos... Family Background and Personal Life Major Shubham Saini hailed from Ghasouli village in Meerut. He was the second of three siblings. His elder brother, Tushar Saini, works in an IT company, while his younger sister, Nidhi Saini, is a teacher at an Army School. His father, Satyendra Saini, is a retired Subedar from the Indian Army. The family was preparing for a wedding, as Major Saini’s elder brother was due to get married on February 18. Speaking to the media, his father said that Shubham had called him just a day before the accident to ask about the wedding preparations and mentioned that he would apply for leave to come home. Army Career Major Saini came from a family deeply connected to the armed forces. After completing his intermediate education from an Army School, he was selected for the National Defence Academy (NDA) in 2015. His passing-out parade was held in Dehradun in 2019. He was commissioned as a Lieutenant and later promoted to the rank of Major. His first posting was in Bathinda, Punjab. His father recalled that Shubham had dreamt of joining the Army since childhood and worked hard both physically and mentally alongside his studies to achieve his goal. Mourning in Village and City Following the news of his death, a wave of grief swept through his village and his residence in Saraswati Vihar on Rohta Road, Meerut. Large numbers of people gathered to pay their respects and offer condolences to the bereaved family. Several social and political figures, including former MLA Jitendra Satwai, Hindu Mahasangh president Mange Sharma, Dr Vikas Khatik, Ankit Rathi and David, expressed deep sorrow over the untimely death of the young Army officer.

stories.title: 6 criminals hold retired clerk's family hostage in Sitapur:Loot jewellery worth ₹50 lakh cash, escape through roof, police forensic team investigates
stories.summary: Criminals took the son and daughter-in-law of a retired Lekhpal hostage and looted jewellery and cash worth 50 lakhs in UP's Sitapur. 6 criminals entered the house through the roof. They held 6 family members hostage at gunpoint. They snatched everyone's mobile phones. Women and men were locked in separate rooms. After this, they kept searching the entire house for an hour. The criminals broke all the boxes and cupboards in the house and looted jewellery worth 45 lakhs along with 5 lakhs in cash. After the robbery, the criminals threatened to kill the family members and fled from the scene. After the criminals left, the victim's family somehow managed to come out. They called the police and informed them about the incident. Police arrived at the scene with a forensic team and dog squad. Evidence was collected by questioning nearby residents. The incident took place in Rasulpur village of the Talgaon police station area. Robbery in house built between fields Amar Singh Verma, a resident of Rasulpur village, was a revenue department clerk. He retired 5 years ago. He owns 45 bighas of land in the village. He had built a house right in the middle of fields, some distance from Basti. There are fields all around. After retirement, Amar moved to his house built in Sitapur. His two sons, Pushkar and Amar, stayed in the village with their families. Both are involved in buying and selling paddy. 6 criminals entered through roof, held hostage at gunpoint Pushkar said that on Saturday, all family members were sleeping after having dinner. Around 3 AM, 6 criminals entered the house through the roof. After this, they went to everyone's rooms one by one and removed their blankets, taking all family members hostage at gunpoint. Took jewellery worth 45 lakhs and 5 lakhs cash The criminals locked the men of the house in one room and the women and children in another room. They took everyone's phones and kept them outside so that no one could contact the police or nearby people. After this, they broke open the almirah and looted my wife's jewellery and my younger brother's wife's jewellery worth about 45 lakhs. They also took 5 lakh rupees cash kept in the almirah. Police-forensic team and dog squad engaged in investigation Upon receiving information, the Talgaon police station reached the spot and started an investigation. The forensic team and dog squad have also reached the spot and are gathering evidence. People in the surrounding area are being questioned, and possible escape routes of the criminals are being investigated. SP Ankur Agrawal said- In Rasulpur village, 5 to 6 miscreants entered the victim's house and committed robbery at gunpoint. In this incident, approximately 4 to 5 lakh rupees in cash and jewelry were looted. Police teams have been deployed and the case will be solved soon. Terror among villagers, demand for increased patrolling Police officials say that the case will be solved soon and the criminals will be arrested. Meanwhile, after the incident, there is an atmosphere of terror in the village and the surrounding areas. Villagers have demanded increased night patrolling and strengthening of security arrangements.

stories.title: Prayagraj student preparing for JEE, dies by suicide:Records apology video before hanging himself; police probe stress factors
stories.summary: A student preparing for the Joint Entrance Exam (JEE) in Prayagraj committed suicide. His body was found hanging from a press wire noose. Before dying, he recorded a video on his mobile. In it, he was crying and saying, "Sorry Papa... I can't study anymore." The incident came to light when the student didn't come out of his room at 11 AM on Saturday. Fellow students knocked on the door but got no response. Then, looking through the window, they found Kuldeep Vishwakarma's body hanging. Police broke down the door to retrieve the body. 25-year-old Kuldeep was from Hamirpur. He had been staying here for a year, preparing for the exam. The entire incident took place in the Saloori area of Colonelganj. Police are investigating whether Kuldeep was under exam pressure or any other kind of stress. The student's family members arrived in Prayagraj today. After this, a post-mortem of the body will be conducted. Kuldeep Vishwakarma lived in a rented room in Salori's Badi Bagiya. He lived alone in the room. According to police, on Saturday morning, Kuldeep did not come out of his room for a long time. At 11 AM, a young man living next door knocked on his room's door, but there was no response from inside. After this, the youth looked inside through the window. Kuldeep was seen hanging from the fan inside the room. After this, the youth immediately informed the students living nearby. People informed the police. Police arrived at the scene and broke down the door to enter the room. Police, with the help of people, brought down student Kuldeep's body from the noose and took him to a nearby hospital. Doctors at the hospital declared him dead. 1-minute video found on mobile Kuldeep's phone was not locked. When police checked the mobile, they found a 1-minute video. In the video, Kuldeep is emotionally apologizing to his parents while crying. Police informed the family about this. The family has asked police not to share the video with anyone. Karnalganj Station In-charge Sanjay Kumar Singh said - Kuldeep hanged himself using a press wire. The body has been kept safely in the postmortem house. The family has been informed, postmortem will be conducted on Sunday after they arrive. Police is investigating the entire matter.
